thread:
Mateo Ruiz: Heads-up — we just got a customer escalation: p99 latency for model cinder-2.1 in us-west1 jumped from ~420ms to ~2.8s over the last hour. They reported failures + timeouts for long-context chat flows.

Priya Shah: Saw the alert too. Any quick flags in the console traces?

Mateo Ruiz: Console trace points to a big slow step in `tokenize()` for requests with > 8k input bytes. The service-level breakdown shows tokenization stage ~1.6s in a bunch of samples.

Jordan Kim: Reproduced a sample locally against staging cinder-2.1 with a long prompt (11k chars). Tokenizer time jumps. Sending log snippet:```
Mateo@staging:/var/log/serve$ grep "tokenize" request-2241.log
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z request=2241 stage=tokenize time_ms=1587
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z request=2241 stage=kv_cache_lookup time_ms=5
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z request=2241 stage=compile time_ms=32
```

Alice Nguyen: Interesting — cinder-2.1 included the new token-merger table (bpe-merge v3) we onboarded last week. Could be an edge-case where certain long sequences cause quadratic behavior in the merge loop.

Lucas Park: I ran a quick diff between cinder-2.0 (good) and cinder-2.1 tokenizer code. There's a new fallback path that attempts iterative re-merge on ambiguous bytes when it hits unknown merges. I suspected it was bounded but tests didn't cover repetitive emoji/ZWJ sequences.

Priya Shah: Customer payload included lots of emoji + mixed CJK, which historically triggers worst-case paths. Can we get a deterministic repro? Mateo, can you paste the failing prompt (sanitized)?

Mateo Ruiz: Paste (sanitized): `Hello 👋🏽 [long conversation with many emojis and CJK characters repeated ~2000 chars]...` Repro curl below:```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"cinder-2.1","input":"[SANITIZED_LONG_EMOJI_CJK]","max_tokens":256}'
```

Jordan Kim: Reproduced locally, CPU shows a hot loop inside `bpe_merge_iterate()` with lots of small allocations. Heap and mem look fine, but time is dominated by tokenizer CPU.

Alice Nguyen: Quick mitigation options: 1) Roll cinder traffic back to 2.0 (safe) 2) Patch tokenizer to short-circuit after N iterations 3) Add a routing rule for long-context requests to use cinder-2.0 or our fallback `redwood/base-1` until fix.

Priya Shah: We should do immediate mitigation 3) plus a quick patch if it’s safe. Routing change is fastest. Ops, can you set a temporary routing rule for requests with input_len > 8k to prefer cinder-2.0?

deploy-bot: Received request to update routing policy. Starting canary: policy-id=rp-8891 canary=10% nodes(us-west1).

Lucas Park: I can open a 1-line change to tokenizer to cap merge-loop iterations at 1k for now (failsafe). It will avoid correctness loss for typical inputs and preserve forward-compat. I'll put up a PR and mark as hotfix.

Mateo Ruiz: Customer confirmed they still see issues — I'll rerun curl pointing to us-west1 after canary finishes.

Jordan Kim: Traces after canary: p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 630ms for canary traffic. Good sign.

Priya Shah: Lucas — how risky is the cap? Any cases where it would materially change output?

Lucas Park: Risk: very small for normal English. For pathological repeated sequences there could be different token boundaries but model output typically stable. We'll call it a temporary safety cap with immediate rollback plan once we have a proper merge-table algorithm fix.

Alice Nguyen: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/9876 — hotfix branch `hotfix/tokenizer-cap`. Includes tests and perf bench.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy successful: commit=9f3c2a hotfix/tokenizer-cap -> nodes(us-west1-canary)

ops-bot: Routing policy rp-8891 updated: long-inputs (>8k bytes) now prefer cinder-2.0; 100% will be applied in 7m if no regressions.

Mateo Ruiz: After the routing rule + canary, customer reports p99 back to ~480ms and no timeouts. Temporarily resolved. 

Priya Shah: Nice. Next steps for permanent fix: 1) Replace naive re-merge with linear-time BPE scanner 2) Add fuzz tests covering emoji+ZWJ+CJK sequences 3) Add perf regression test for long input tokenization time in CI 4) Add a tokenization-stage timeout heuristic in runtime to avoid 1.5s stalls.

Lucas Park: I'll own 1 + 2. Planning to benchmark against real customer payloads. Estimated ETA: 3 business days for prototype, 1 week for final tested patch.

Jordan Kim: I'll add CI perf job change for step 3 and the runtime heuristic (4). Prefers config flag for TTL so we can tune.

Mateo Ruiz: Logging action items in support ticket and cc'ing customer-facing notes. They asked for a short postmortem and ETA.

Priya Shah: Also let's add a fallback model rule in Console per-route: if tokenization stage > 1s then route remainder of session to a compatible model variant. That will reduce customer-visible tail latency while we fix.

Alice Nguyen: Agreed. I'll add the fallback policy config to the roll plan.

deploy-bot: Full rollout of hotfix scheduled at 2026-03-15T15:10Z pending smoke tests.

Mateo Ruiz: Closing loop with customer: "We've applied a routing mitigation and a canary hotfix. We are implementing a permanent tokenizer fix; ETA ~1 week. Will share follow-up once merged."

Priya Shah: Follow-ups: add fuzz suite, add a perf regression alert tied to tokenizer time (p95/p99), and schedule a knowledge-share on BPE corner cases.

Lucas Park: Pushed initial PR for prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizer/pull/214 (WIP). Benchmarks show ~6x improvement on pathological case.

Jordan Kim: I'll create an incident note and mark severity as S2 (customer impact p99) with the timeline + mitigations.

Mateo Ruiz: Thanks all. I'll keep thread open until the PR is merged and customer confirms green. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Hotfix rollout complete. smoke=OK.

ops-bot: Routing policy rp-8891 now fully active.

Mateo Ruiz: Customer emailed back: "Thanks, latency is back to normal and we're unblocked." Marking as resolved for now; follow-up postmortem will be added to postmortems/ with root cause and lessons learned. :wave:
